This matter is taken up through Hybrid mode.
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State-Opposite Party.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail relating to Chauliaganj P.S. Case No.187 of 2024, corresponding to G.R. Case No.795 of 2014, pending before the learned J.M.F.C.-IV (Cog. Taking), Cuttack, for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 506 & 34 of IPC.
4.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that earlier this matter was not before any other Bench of this Court.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is in custody since 24.08.2024.
She further contended that the investigation has progressed substantially and the final charge-sheet is likely to be filed soon.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that as per allegation of the FIR, the present Petitioner, who happens to be the owner of a Xerox shop, has prepared fake documents.
She further contended that the principal accused in the present case is one Prasanna @ Parshuram Bhoi.
It was further submitted that although the Petitioner is having two criminal antecedents, however, he is ready and willing to abide by any terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State on the other hand contended that the allegations made in the FIR are grave and serious in nature.

It was further contended that the Petitioner is having similar criminal antecedents, therefore, in the event he is released on bail there is every possibility he might abscond from justice which would eventually cause delay in conclusion of the investigation as well as filing of the charge-sheet.
In such view of the matter, it is submitted that the prayer for bail of the Petitioner be rejected at this juncture.

6. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on careful consideration of the surrounding facts as well as materials on record, and the period of custodial detention, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.35,000/- (Rupees Thirty Five Thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned court in seisin over the matter.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
7. It is further directed that the bail granted to the Petitioner is subject to the condition that the court below shall verify whether the Petitioner is having similar criminal antecedent.
In the event it is found that the Petitioner is having more than two similar criminal antecedents, this bail order shall automatically stand revoked.

8. It is further directed that the bail granted to the Petitioner is subject to depositing of a cash security of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand) before the learned Court in seisin over the matter,
which shall be kept in any Nationalized Bank in interest bearing account initially for a period of one year which will be renewable from time to time till conclusion of trial and the same shall be abide by the final outcome of the trial of the case.
9.
The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.

( Aditya Kumar Mohapatra)
 Judge S.K. Rout
